digest.component_or_area: snapshot janitor and root disk pressure mitigation
propositions: The snapshot janitor's free-space reclaim trigger uses an absolute 2 GiB floor that is disk-size-blind, crossing only at 93.3% used on a 30 GiB volume, above the 85% alarm threshold and the 90% peak reached during the incident.

Every review materializes a full ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree keyed on a ref that advances every ~26 seconds with minimal delta, creating a ~0.85 GiB per review append-only pattern instead of a cached store, at a measured rate of 4.4 GiB/h.

The snapshot store resides on the container writable layer (30 GiB root disk) because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset everywhere, causing store_root() to fall through to tempfile.gettempdir() instead of using the separate /var/gerrit EBS volume.

Runtime injection of free-space values shows the janitor evicts zero entries at both 85% used (4.50 GiB free) and 90% used (3.00 GiB free) on a 30 GiB volume, first engaging only past 93.3% used where reclaim is already too late.

The 7-day cold-trim eviction predicate is unreachable because the container is recreated every few hours (23 times in 4 days), and the byte-total backstop promised by the ADR and module docstring is never implemented in _gc_pass.

The fix adds a volume-relative percentage-based watermark term (MAX(absolute_floor, volume * pct // 100)) with hysteresis to a reclaim target margin, defaulting to 0 (off) but set to 20 in the review-bot compose service to engage reclaim at 80% used, below the 85% alarm floor.
